EQUIVALENT SPELL LEVEL: (5 x Ability)
PENETRATION TOTAL: Casting Total + Penetration Bonus — Ease Factor
MAXIMUM VIS EXPENDITURE: Ability + Effect Vis Cost

entries.title: Folk Witch Casting Methods
entries.summary: Each Ability must be used by Potion, Incantation (a rhyme the target hears) or Fetish (a prepared item), with rules for losing the incantation from memory and for spare fetishes.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 6 for her every day after the memory-altering effect ceases

entries.title: Folk Witch Botches
entries.summary: A botch makes the effect happen uncontrolled and gives the witch Warping Points.
quotes: She also gains 1 Warping Point for every 0 on the botch dice

entries.title: Folk Witch Mark
entries.summary: Each witch's effects carry a personal mark that others can recognize with a Perception and Organization Lore roll; identifying merely that a witch cast it is easier.
quotes: make a Perception + Organization Lore: Folk Witch roll against an Ease Factor of 9
a successful Perception + Organization Lore: Folk Witch roll against an Ease Factor of 6 identifies an effect as one cast by a Folk Witch

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Animal Ken
entries.summary: Folk witch Animal Ken uses Communication and the Animal Form, delivered by incantation or potion.
quotes: Characteristic: Communication

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Cursing (and the curses)
entries.summary: A witch curses a target via a woven fetish or potion, using Dexterity and a Form that depends on the curse; each curse type (disease, miscarriage, aging, emotion, tongue, paralysis, beast, reduction) has its own Ease Factor and effect, and the curse must penetrate the target's Magic Resistance throughout the preparation season.
quotes: Preparing the curse is a laboratory activity that takes the folk witch an entire season
use the highest Magic Resistance the target has during the season

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Dowsing
entries.summary: Folk witch Dowsing uses Perception, a Form that depends on the target, and a fetish or potion; it lets witches find vis.
quotes: This ability is important for folk witches as it allows them to find vis.

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Flight
entries.summary: A witch can fly using Stamina and Auram, at the cost of a long-term Fatigue level when using a fetish; it describes speed, duration, maneuver rolls and a combat bonus against non-flying opponents.
quotes: The Ease Factor to take to the air is 9.
her Flight Ability score is added to both her Attack and Defense Totals

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Healing
entries.summary: True healing of wounds and Fatigue that breaks the Limit of Energy; it costs Corpus vis according to a table of Ease Factors by wound or fatigue level, and must penetrate the target's Magic Resistance.
quotes: the folk witch must spend a number of pawns of Corpus vis depending on the wound type (indicated below)

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Second Sight
entries.summary: Folk witch Second Sight uses Perception and the Vim Form, delivered by incantation or potion.
quotes: Form: Vim

entries.title: Folk Witch Ability: Shapeshifter
entries.summary: Folk witch Shapeshifter uses Stamina and the Animal Form, delivered by fetish (made from the animal's skin) or potion.
quotes: The fetish is made from the skin of the animal form.

entries.title: Folk Witch Magic Theory
entries.summary: An Arcane Ability analogous to Magic Theory, covering the technical details of folk witch magic and used in kitchen laboratory activities; any character can be taught it.
quotes: Any character can be taught this Ability.

entries.title: Folk Witch Study
entries.summary: Studying in the kitchen gives no bonus, and learning Supernatural Abilities remains difficult or impossible for unGifted witches without an existing score.

entries.title: Potion Effects
entries.summary: What each Ability's potion does for the drinker: temporary Ability scores and durations derived from the Brew Potency, curse potions, healing potions and shapeshifting.
quotes: with an Ability score equal to the Brew Potency / 5 (round up)

entries.title: Covens
entries.summary: A coven is the folk witch equivalent of a covenant: a small, dispersed group of witches, each living a day's travel apart, with its strengths and vulnerabilities.

entries.title: Sabbat
entries.summary: The coven meeting where witches trade vis and discuss threats; because witches lack Parma Magica the Gift's social effects often cause bickering, and a sabbat does not interrupt long-term tasks.

entries.title: Sabbat Politics
entries.summary: Four optional ways a sabbat can run (Easy, Bickering, Dictatorial, Feuding), depending on the Gifted makeup of the coven and the kind of stories wanted.

entries.title: Sabbat Times
entries.summary: A table of the traditional dates on which covens hold sabbats, grouped under the winter and summer solstices.

entries.title: Curse-Throwing
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to cure diseases, lift curses and dispel harmful effects by transferring them to another person, with a Casting Total against an Ease Factor by affliction type, ritual time, Penetration and modifiers for how the recipient is represented; includes a worked example.
quotes: Curse-Throwing Casting Total: Presence + Curse-Throwing + Aura + stress die
Penetration Total: Casting Total – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus

entries.title: Charms
entries.summary: Explains how a Virtue can be tied to a secret faerie charm through the Charm Flaws, how the charm is lost if shared, and which Virtues may be charmed.
quotes: The Virtue must affect what the character can do, not who he is.
if other characters become party to the charm, the power vanishes like mist in the sunlight

entries.title: Folk Charms
entries.summary: Hedge-magic charm that ends a faerie effect, rolled with Intelligence and Faerie Lore, at the cost of a Fatigue level and a Warping point.
quotes: stress die + Intelligence + Faerie Lore + aura
Activating a folk charm costs a Fatigue level and gives the character a point of Warping.

entries.title: Hermetic Charms
entries.requires: Sympathy Trait gained from exposure to the Faerie realm
entries.summary: Lets a magus apply Sympathy Traits to Hermetic Abilities, Lab Totals, talisman attunement and charmed devices, and treat the work as a Magic or Faerie effect for Realm Interaction.
quotes: Sympathy Traits can be used as specializations to boost Abilities used to perform Hermetic magic, including Penetration and Magic Theory.
he may add the value of any of his Sympathy Traits that are appropriate to the shape or material to his Lab Total

entries.title: Examples of Charmed Virtues
entries.summary: Sidebar giving example Virtues with the charm that activates each.

entries.title: Faerie Ceremony
entries.summary: A Faerie Supernatural Ability that lets a group join a focus character in a faerie effect, adding a group modifier and each participant's Characteristic plus Ability or Method to the focus character's total.
quotes: Group Modifier: total Ceremony scores – number of participants

entries.title: Learning Faerie Abilities
entries.requires: Strong alignment to the Faerie realm (Sympathy Traits and Faerie Rank)
entries.summary: Describes how characters aligned to Faerie learn Faerie Supernatural Abilities and Arts like Gifted characters learn Magic Abilities, with experience limited by Faerie Rank and easier study of a tradition's four Favored Abilities.
quotes: the sum of the character's strongest positive and negative Sympathy Traits must equal at least 5 at the start of the season for him to learn a new Ability in this way

related.text: ArM5 p.166 Gifted characters learning Magic Abilities

entries.title: Faerie Wizardry Overview
entries.summary: Introduces faerie wizards, or faerie hedge wizards, who use faerie rites and faerie bargaining, and the traditions that teach their Abilities and Arts.

entries.title: Rites of Faerie
entries.requires: Faerie Method, Faerie Power and Sympathy Trait
entries.summary: Introduces faerie rites, spontaneous spell-like effects that faerie wizards focus through a Faerie Method and Power.

entries.title: Performing Faerie Rites
entries.requires: Faerie Method, Faerie Power and Sympathy Trait
entries.summary: Procedure for casting a faerie rite: the stress die plus Characteristic, Method, Power and aura gives the level, capped by the applicable Sympathy Traits, with rules for negative Traits, botches, experience, ritual-level rites and the lack of permanent effects.
quotes: Rite Casting Total: stress die + Characteristic + Method + Power + aura modifier
Maximum Rite Level: (Sympathy Traits x 5)

related.text: ArM5 pp.111-114 Hermetic Ranges, Durations and Targets

entries.title: Hermetic Rites
entries.summary: Allows a magus with a Faerie Method and Power to design Hermetic rituals using faerie rite guidelines and the special Faerie Ranges, Durations and Targets, using Method and Power in place of Artes Liberales and Philosophiae.
quotes: the caster may add his scores in the Method and Power instead of Artes Liberales and Philosophiae to his Casting Total

entries.title: Faerie Ranges, Durations, and Targets
entries.requires: Faerie wizard: Faerie Method, Faerie Power and Sympathy Trait
entries.summary: Sidebar of extra Ranges (Crossroads, Presence, Prop, Symbol), Durations (Held, Focus, While, Geas, Hour + 1, Midday/Midnight, Not, Season, Aura, Faerie, Hidden, If, Symbol) and Targets (Medium, Passion, Symbol) available to faerie rites, with their equivalent spell levels and conditions.
quotes: Anyone with a total of 6 or higher is affected.

related.text: ArM5 pp.111-114 Hermetic Ranges, Durations, Targets
ArM5 pp.92-93 House Merinita Faerie Magic

entries.title: Faerie Methods
entries.requires: Faerie wizard: Faerie Method, Faerie Power and Sympathy Trait
entries.summary: Explains that Methods are Supernatural Abilities used with a Faerie Power to perform a rite, and gives guidance for designing new Methods with a Characteristic, a cost and an advantage.

entries.title: Evocation (Faerie Method)
entries.summary: Faerie Method using Communication that calls on faerie patrons at the cost of a Warping Point or Confidence Point, and lets the user add vis to any rite for a bonus with a limit and botch risk.
quotes: with each pawn spent increasing his Rite Casting Total by 2.

entries.title: Enchantment (Faerie Method)
entries.summary: Faerie Method using Presence in which the user performs an Ability roll against an Ease Factor tied to the intended magnitude, building up a bonus over several rounds before casting the rite; can also roll a simple die to avoid botching.
quotes: making a roll against an Ease Factor of (the magnitude of the intended effect x 3)

entries.title: Empathy (Faerie Method)
entries.summary: Faerie Method using Stamina that requires spending a Fatigue level on a lengthy trance ritual, and lets the user spend more Fatigue to extend the rite, reset bonus limits and multiply the effect cap from Sympathy Traits.
quotes: Empathy allows him to effectively double the value of the Sympathy Traits that determine his effect level

entries.title: Pagan Traditions
entries.summary: Introduces faerie hedge wizard traditions, with Favored Abilities that are easier to learn, Initiation Scripts, and the minimum Virtue points and Sympathy Traits needed to build a starting faerie wizard.
quotes: the player must devote at least four points of the character's starting Virtues to a Faerie Method and a Faerie Power

related.text: Chapter 5: Touches of Faerie, Learning Supernatural Abilities

entries.title: Borrowers
entries.summary: Faerie bargaining tradition of travelling traders who sell goods to faeries; Favored Arts are Summoning, Bonding, Captivating and Dismissing.
quotes: Summoning, Bonding, Captivating, Dismissing

entries.title: Ollamhain
entries.summary: Irish poet-sage tradition of faerie wizardry; Favored Abilities are Enchantment, Beguile, Dream and Portage.
quotes: Enchantment, Beguile, Dream, Portage

entries.title: Volkhvy
entries.summary: Russian pagan faerie wizards who work communal rites; Favored Abilities are Evocation, Ceremony, Conjure and Grant.
quotes: Evocation, Ceremony, Conjure, Grant

entries.title: Wise Folk
entries.summary: Village wise men and women who ward off the supernatural and mend or injure; Favored Abilities are Empathy, Ware, Weal and Woe.
quotes: Empathy, Ware, Weal, Woe

entries.title: Hunters' Arts (Practice and Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Overview of the Hunters' Arts, a splintered hedge tradition with three Practice Arts (Scry, Ban, Slay) each paired with a Foe Art. Explains how the Arts are bought as Virtues, how the first Foe Art comes free, how experience is gained and why most hunters can only use their Arts on one kind of foe.
quotes: There are three Practices that are akin to Hermetic Techniques: Scry, Ban, and Slay.

Practice Arts are bought as Major Supernatural Virtues, whereas Foe Arts are Minor Supernatural Virtues, but a character buying his first Practice Art as a Virtue gets one free Foe Art at no additional Virtue point cost.

entries.title: The Hunters' Arts and Mortal Foes
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining that Hunters' Arts also work on humans and creatures aligned to a Realm but lacking Might, at a raised effect level.
quotes: Against such mortal foes, the levels of all effects are 10 higher.

entries.title: Penetration and the Hunters' Arts
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Gives the Penetration Total formula used by every Hunters' Art and notes that hunters rely on Arcane and sympathetic connections to foes.
quotes: Penetration Total: Art Total + Penetration Bonus – Level

entries.title: (Foe) Art (Virtue and rules for Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Describes the Foe Art Virtue: what counts as a valid foe, the storyguide's say over its breadth, and that Foe Arts are Difficult Arts that advance like Abilities and must be combined with a Practice Art.
quotes: A foe must have some supernatural power: wholly mundane groups cannot be foes.
(Foe) Arts are Difficult Arts, meaning that they are treated as any other Art except that they use the Ability Advancement Table rather than the Art Advancement Table.

entries.title: Connections to a Foe (sympathetic and arcane connection tables)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Sidebar tables of extra sympathetic connection bonuses and arcane connection durations and multipliers commonly used in the Hunters' Arts, such as names, wounds, graves and the vampire's children.
quotes: in addition to those in ArM5, page 84

entries.title: Scry Art: Forging the Initial Connection
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: How a hunter makes a Scry roll to connect to a foe, with a table of Scry Levels giving direction, senses and sympathetic bonuses by strength, Range and mortal-foe adjustments, botch consequences, and how connections are replaced or cancelled.
quotes: Scry Total: Perception + Scry + (Foe) + Aura bonus + stress die
Add 10 levels (not magnitudes) if the foe lacks a Might score.

entries.title: Scry Art: Using the Scrying Connection
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: Once a connection exists the hunter concentrates for a round and makes a non-magical roll against an Ease Factor set by the foe's strength to sense it.
quotes: Sense a Foe: Stamina + Concentration + stress die
Ease Factor: 6 + (foe's Might/5)

entries.title: Scry Art: Exploitation of Scry by a Foe
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: How a foe may detect and exploit a scryer's connection: an Awareness roll against a falling Ease Factor, and then using Eye, Sight or Arcane range powers on the scryer through an Arcane Connection.
quotes: The Ease Factor starts at 12, but decreases by 1 every time the scryer uses her connection to find the foe.

entries.title: Ban Art (warding amulets overview)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Introduces the Ban Art and its three amulets (Physical, Supernatural and Weakening Bans), noting that only the highest Ban protects a person and that Magic Resistance can nullify an amulet.
quotes: A character cannot be protected by more than one Physical or Supernatural Ban; only the one with the highest Ban Total takes effect.

entries.title: Creating a Physical Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Amulet that absorbs wounds from a foe: made over twelve hours with a Sun Duration, its Ban Strength is spent by wound severity per a table until exhausted, with a worked example.
quotes: Physical Ban Total: Presence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura modifier + stress die
Physical Ban Strength: Physical Ban Total – Level
It takes twelve continuous hours to create a Physical Ban, and it has a Sun Duration.

entries.title: Creating a Supernatural Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Single-use amulet that partly protects against a foe's powers by shortening durations and forcing extra Concentration rolls, with three Levels of effect; mortal foes add to the Level.
quotes: Supernatural Ban Total: Intelligence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura modifier + stress die

entries.title: Creating a Weakening Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Area ward laid out with prepared hawthorn stakes that suppresses a foe's Might Score while it is inside, with rules for the number of stakes, activation, the roll and Penetration.
quotes: Weakening Ban Total: Intelligence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura bonus + stress die
The minimum number of stakes is one per 16 paces of the diameter of a circle, rounded up.

entries.title: Slay Art: Making the Slaying Weapon
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: How a hunter turns a fresh weapon into a one-use foe-slayer in a day, paying a Long Term Fatigue level, with a Slay Total, a Level lowered by correct facts about the foe and raised by wrong ones, and an Incapacitating Wound effect on a successful strike.
quotes: Slay Total: Dexterity + Slay + (Foe) + Aura + stress die
It takes one day (24 hours) of continuous work to turn a normal weapon into a tool of foe-slaying, and costs the slayer one Long Term Fatigue level.
The Level is decreased by five points (to a minimum of 5, or 15 for mortal Foes) for every correct fact about the foe that the slayer has been able to discover.

entries.title: Relevant Facts About Foes
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: Sidebar listing the kinds of facts about a foe that count toward lowering the Slay Level.

entries.title: After Slaying
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: A slaying weapon loses all magic after it is used or after its foe dies by other means, and can never be enchanted again.

entries.title: Working Together (hunter teamwork and Hermetic cooperation)
entries.summary: Sidebar on how the different hunter types and Practice Arts complement each other, and how hunters can help Hermetic magi, for example by weakening foes so spells Penetrate more easily.
quotes: the Slay Art does not destroy the vis in a creature's body like some Perdo Vim spells can

entries.title: Debauchery (Ability)
entries.summary: The Unholy Method of focusing will through a strenuous physical act, at the cost of a long-term Fatigue level or a Light Wound, using Stamina for the maleficium roll.
quotes: calls upon her Stamina for the maleficium roll

entries.title: Incantation (Ability)
entries.summary: The Unholy Method of invoking Infernal power through chanted or written blasphemy, adding Communication to the roll and costing a Confidence point.
quotes: requires that he spend a point of Confidence to call the effect into being

entries.title: Maleficia (Infernal casting)
entries.requires: Infernalist with a Method and a Power
entries.summary: Core rules for casting Infernal effects: combine a Method and a Power in a stress-die total against a target level, with failures costing botches and Warping, Hierarchy softening the consequences, a season to secure a soul after a botch, and the Vengeful Powers penalty for selfless use.
quotes: Maleficium: stress die + Characteristic + Method + Power + aura bonus
Treat a failed roll as one botch for each ten levels or fraction thereof that the infernalist is lacking.
The infernalist may substitute his (Hierarchy Score x 10) for his Maleficium Total

entries.title: Infernal Ranges, Durations, and Targets
entries.summary: New spell parameters for maleficia: Range Crossroads, Duration Cursed (condition), Duration Forsaken and Target Passion, each with its equivalent magnitude.
quotes: Range Crossroads is considered the same level as Range Voice.
Duration Forsaken is the same level as Duration Year
Target Passion is the same level as Target Group

related.text: ArM5 p.92 Faerie Magic Range: Road

entries.title: Debauchery (Unholy Method)
entries.summary: The Method of casting a maleficium through a corrupting ritual that costs a long-term Fatigue level or a Light Wound, using Stamina, and that can be extended over hours or a whole season to build up Confidence spending or add Infernal Lore.
quotes: This uses the character's Stamina with the maleficium roll.

entries.title: Example: Richard of Glastonbury (maleficium)
entries.summary: A worked example of building and casting a maleficium, computing a casting total, rolling a possible botch and spending Confidence to limit the damage.
quotes: This is a base 15 Incantation/Diablerie effect

entries.title: Powerful Maleficia
entries.summary: Lists the ways an infernalist can boost a maleficium total: Ceremony, Confidence, Hierarchy, Sacrifice and vis, and that they can be combined.

entries.title: Incantation (Unholy Method)
entries.summary: The Method of casting through chanted words, using Communication, costing a Confidence Point or a Warping Point, and allowing infernal vis to boost the casting total.
quotes: Each pawn of vis he expends while casting the maleficium gives him a +2 bonus to his casting total
The number of pawns he can use in a single maleficium is limited to his (Incantation + Power).

entries.title: New Methods and Powers
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on designing additional Methods and Powers for maleficia, including the minimum pairings and how to adapt an existing Method.
quotes: each new Method must be associated with at least two Powers, and each new Power must use at least one Method

entries.title: Unholy Powers (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the six unholy Powers, each combined with an unholy Method to form an effect, with guidelines per combination.
quotes: There are six unholy Powers

entries.title: Consumption (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power of drawing on the life and health of living beings: Debauchery reshapes the body, Incantation steals life from others, and failure deforms the caster.

entries.title: Diablerie (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power of influencing demons and other supernatural beings within range, and how Forsaken Duration effects become Infernal blessings treated as Vengeful Powers.
quotes: Diablerie maleficia that grant Powers to the target are usually Forsaken Duration

entries.title: Effusion (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power over base materials and insubstantial forces: Debauchery governs fire, air and unseen forces, Incantation governs water, earth and cold matter. It cannot create anything living or make something from nothing.
quotes: Effusion cannot produce anything living

entries.title: Malediction (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power of cursing: Incantation lays general curses, Debauchery lays destructive ones, with Infernal curses usually Forsaken in Duration, bad-luck side effects for roll penalties, and backfire on failure.
quotes: usually have a Forsaken Duration, so that they remain active until the victim can somehow dispel them

entries.title: Phantasm (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power of Infernal illusions that seem real: Debauchery conjures or transforms into phantasms, Incantation perceives and predicts. Phantasms are dispelled by the Divine, cannot survive in the Dominion, and are vulnerable to a chosen material.
quotes: Phantasms cannot survive in the Dominion.
If a phantasm is somehow affected by the Divine, it is immediately dispelled

entries.title: Psychomachia (Unholy Power)
entries.summary: Describes the Power over mind and emotion: Incantation reads and controls minds, Debauchery changes personality so the target wants to sin, and failure muddles the caster.
quotes: with Debauchery the caster can change the target's personality

entries.title: Storm Wizards (hedge tradition)
entries.summary: Introduces the Transylvanian storm wizards, a rare Gifted hedge tradition whose apprentices are found as exposed infants on mountain slopes and taken by storm giants. Almost all are male and live alone in caves above the snowline.
quotes: The Transylvanian storm wizards are an old but lonely Gifted tradition.

entries.title: Storm Wizards and the Order
entries.summary: Explains how the Order of Hermes regards storm wizards: few know of them, the join-or-die Code provision technically applies because they are Gifted, and some joined House Ex Miscellanea during the Schism War.
quotes: As storm wizards are Gifted, the "join or die" provisions of the Code technically apply to them.

entries.title: Storm Wizards and Giants (Giant Blood and the mystery initiation)
entries.summary: Storm wizards get the Giant Blood Virtue free, earned by a mystery initiation at the end of apprenticeship in which the apprentice slays a giant and eats its heart. Powers are usable as soon as the Gift is opened, before the initiation.
quotes: If you are making a storm wizard character, this Virtue is free.
storm wizards undergo a mystery initiation in which they must slay a true giant and eat his heart

entries.title: Heart of the Storm Initiation
entries.requires: Initiation: Heart of the Storm (Storm Wizards)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the initiation ease factor, initiation total formula and script bonus for the storm wizard initiation that grants Giant Blood.
quotes: Initiation Ease Factor: 21
Presence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizards + Script Bonus

entries.title: Storm Wizard Magic
entries.summary: Overview of storm wizard magic: exclusively Gifted, Magic-realm powers built on three Supernatural Abilities, an Arcane Ability and a seasonal activity called ice harvesting.
quotes: Their magic consists of three favored Supernatural Abilities: Storm Calling, Storm Riding, and Storm Fighting.

entries.title: Storm Wizard Virtues and Abilities
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining that storm wizards gain their Supernatural Abilities at Score 0 when the Gift is opened, and giving the Storm Calling, Storm Riding and Storm Fighting Virtues, the free Storm Wizard status and the Organization Lore: Storm Wizard Arcane Ability.
quotes: Opening Total is generated as Intelligence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizards

entries.title: Storm Calling (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to create or move a storm: a roll against an Ease Factor set by the storm's size and duration, plus Auram vis sacrificed to create one. Created storms are natural once formed, and moving one costs no vis.
quotes: Storm Calling Roll: Communication + Storm Calling + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
It takes a number of rounds equal to the required Ease Factor for the storm to manifest.

entries.title: Storm Calling Ease Factors (storm size, duration and vis cost)
entries.summary: Sidebar table of the Ease Factor modifiers for storm size and duration and the Auram vis cost per size, with a worked example of creating and moving a provincial storm.
quotes: The Base Ease Factor for creating and moving a storm is 0.

entries.title: Penetration with Storm Wizard Powers
entries.summary: How Penetration is figured for storm wizard powers, using the effect roll minus the Ease Factor plus a Penetration Bonus built as for Hermetic magi, with access to the Penetration Ability.
quotes: Penetration: Storm Wizard Effect Roll – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus

entries.title: Magnitude of Storm Wizard Effects
entries.summary: States how to determine the magnitude of a storm wizard power when it matters, for example for Warping or dispelling.
quotes: Magnitude: Storm Wizard Supernatural Ability Score

entries.title: Realm Interaction for Storm Wizard Powers
entries.summary: Storm wizard powers are Magical Supernatural Abilities and take bonuses or penalties from the local aura per the Realm Interaction Table.

entries.title: Storm Trance: Warping
entries.summary: When a storm wizard gains Warping Points, a Storm Trance roll may turn him into a local-sized storm for a Moon, during which he cannot use his powers and can try daily to reform. Failure to reform can kill him or send him into the Magic Realm.
quotes: Storm Trance Roll: Strength + Stress Die
Storm Trance Ease Factor: 3 + Warping Score

entries.title: Inside the Storm
entries.summary: Rule of thumb for deciding when a character counts as within a storm for storm wizard powers: being rained on or blown about by it, not merely being inside a building.

entries.title: Storm Riding (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to sense from, or instantly travel to, any point in a visible storm (or send another character there), with a +3 bonus when the wizard is inside the storm and three ease factors by effect.
quotes: Storm Riding Roll: Perception + Storm Riding + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
he receives a +3 bonus to the Storm Riding roll if he is actually inside the storm when he uses the Ability

entries.title: Storm Fighting (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to attack with a storm, with five attack types (Buffet, Deluge, Hail, Erosion, Lightning), each with its own Ease Factor, area, damage and Penetration rules.
quotes: Storm Fighting Roll: Strength + Storm Fighting + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
Lightning: Ease Factor 12.

entries.title: Ice Harvesting (seasonal activity)
entries.summary: A season-long ritual that gathers the magical non-melting ice storm wizards need as Auram vis to call storms, gathered at secret mountain sites. The vis yield comes from a formula using Intelligence, Organization Lore and the Magic aura.
quotes: (Intelligence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizard + Magic Aura) / 3 (round up) pawns of Auram vis per season

entries.title: Ars Notoria (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the Notory Art of King Solomon, a Christian system of orations and figures (notae) combined into rings that grant divinely given knowledge and abilities; only Gifted Christians can use it.

entries.title: Finding a Text of the Ars Notoria
entries.summary: A character can seek a copy of the Ars Notoria through a story or, less entertainingly, spend a season rolling Intelligence + Divine Lore against a high Ease Factor; a botch turns up some other book.
quotes: FINDING A COPY OF ARS NOTORIA: Intelligence + Divine Lore + stress die vs. an Ease Factor of 21

entries.title: Studying the Ars Notoria
entries.summary: Learning the Ability from the text requires reading four languages and Artes Liberales, a Gifted reader and the normal rules for learning a Supernatural Ability; starting characters must take it as a Major Supernatural Virtue.
quotes: The reader needs a 4 in each Language to accurately read the book.
The Ars Notoria text is treated as a tractatus with a Quality of 20.

entries.title: Ars Notoria: Future Study
entries.summary: Ars Notoria is increased by study like other Abilities; glosses help with understanding but cannot teach the Ability initially.

entries.title: The Rings of Solomon (recitation rules)
entries.summary: Explains how rings are recited: a recitation score plus a stress die against an Ease Factor depending on ring level and duration, season-long first recitations, learning rings in order, no stacking of benefits, and tracking temporary experience.
quotes: RECITATION SCORE: Intelligence + Ars Notoria + Modifier
FIRST RECITATION OF AN ARS NOTORIA RING: Ease Factor = 6 + 3 times level of ring + 1 per season of desired duration
SUBSEQUENT RECITATIONS OF A KNOWN ARS NOTORIA RING: Ease Factor = 3 + 3 times level of ring + 1 per season of desired duration

entries.title: Ars Notoria Modifiers
entries.summary: Table of modifiers to the recitation score for behavior such as fasting, chastity, personality Flaws, sins and conflicting Supernatural Abilities, with explanations including the fasting roll.
quotes: Characters wishing to fast for a season must make a Stamina + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 6 to succeed.
| Performing a Mortal Sin| –9 |

entries.title: First Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: First ring, recited in spring or autumn, grants temporary experience in Philosophiae and raises Communication.
quotes: Successfully reciting this oration gives you 100 experience points in the Academic Ability: Philosophiae.

entries.title: Second Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Second ring, recited in winter, grants temporary experience in Theology and raises Intelligence.
quotes: With a successful recitation of the second ring, you gain 100 experience points in the Academic Ability: Theology.

entries.title: Third Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Third ring, recitable in any season, grants temporary experience in Medicine and the Greater Purifying Touch Virtue for a chosen disease.
quotes: A person gains 100 experience points in the Academic Ability: Medicine, and also receives for free the Supernatural Major Virtue: Greater Purifying Touch.

entries.title: Fourth Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Fourth ring summons a personal patron angel who acts as a guardian and teacher of academic Abilities, and may end the ring or cancel other rings if the character acts impiously.
quotes: Successfully reciting the fourth ring grants you the Major General Virtue: Patron Angel.

entries.title: Fifth Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Fifth ring, recited in summer, lets the character determine which realm a being is affiliated with and possibly learn its powers, with no need to Penetrate.
quotes: SENSE REALM AFFILIATION: Perception + Ars Notoria vs. 6 + Target's Magic Resistance/5

entries.title: Sixth Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Sixth ring, recited in spring, provides holy divination about the results of actions via a Perception + Ars Notoria roll against difficulties listed in a table.
quotes: DIVINATION: Perception + Ars Notoria vs. variable Ease Factor

entries.title: Seventh Ring of Solomon
entries.summary: Seventh ring gives perfect understanding of known skills: simple die rolls become stress dice and stress dice cannot botch, though the patron angel may end it for Pride.
quotes: In game terms, you replace all your simple die rolls with stress die rolls.

entries.title: Ars Notoria: Beneficial Side-Effects
entries.summary: Ars Notoria score reduces the Divine-aura penalty to other magic and an active ring prevents Warping Points from Divine auras.
quotes: For each point of Ars Notoria you have, you may reduce the Divine penalty received from the Realm Interaction Chart by 3.

entries.title: Ars Notoria: Writing Books
entries.summary: Rules caveats for writing books while a ring's benefits are active: the effect must cover the writing period, authors cannot stop to extend it, and cannot learn from their own texts.
quotes: Remember too that no author may learn from his own texts.

entries.title: Secrets of the Necromancer
entries.summary: Introduces Canaanite necromancy as a Major Supernatural Virtue and matching Supernatural Ability, noting that learning it from the ghost of Zephaniah is impractical for magi and that integration into Hermetic theory is the realistic route.

entries.title: Major Supernatural Virtue: Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: A Canaanite necromancer replicates Hermetic Corpus or Mentem effects dealing with communicating with, commanding or summoning the dead using a stress roll against an Ease Factor scaled to the effect's magnitude, and can use the Veil of Death range.
quotes: A stress roll of Communication + Canaanite Necromancy Ability against an Ease Factor of (3 x the magnitude of the effect)
Communication + Canaanite Necromancy Ability + stress die vs. Ease Factor (3 x magnitude of effect)

entries.title: Hermetic Integration (Canaanite Necromancy)
entries.summary: A magus working with a Canaanite necromancer assistant gains Insight Lab Texts and invents effects dealing with the dead, accumulating breakthrough points until the Minor Hermetic Virtue Canaanite Magic is gained.
quotes: To Integrate Canaanite Necromancy: Accumulate 45 or more breakthrough points

entries.title: Canaanite Laboratory Assistants
entries.summary: A Canaanite necromancer can supply the Insight and assist with experimental effects during integration, adding to the magus's Lab Total, but only for projects integrating Canaanite and Hermetic practice.
quotes: The magus receives a bonus to his Lab Total equal to the necromancer's Intelligence + Canaanite Necromancy Ability score

entries.title: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Canaanite Magic
entries.summary: The integrated Virtue grants the Veil of Death range, a permanent Arcane Connection to all the dead with a Penetration bonus, and in return the dead always sense the magus and hold an Arcane Connection to him.
quotes: exploit this Arcane Connection for a +4 Penetration multiplier bonus
a simple Perception roll against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: New Range: Veil of Death
entries.requires: Virtue: Canaanite Magic or Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: A new spell Range that reaches any dead mortal human regardless of the distance to their remains, provided the caster is connected to the target; it counts as Sight for magnitude purposes.
quotes: For the purposes of spell magnitudes, this range is equivalent to Sight.

entries.title: Who is Dead?
entries.requires: Virtue: Canaanite Magic or Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: Defines which dead can be reached by Canaanite necromancy (mortals not yet in Heaven, ghosts) and which cannot (animals, faeries, Final Twilight), and doubles botch dice when targeting those given a Divine burial rite.
quotes: if the caster botches double the number of botch dice are rolled

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine (extreme unction)

entries.title: Speaking to the Dead
entries.requires: Virtue: Canaanite Magic or Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: Advice on the limits of conversing with the long dead: mutual incomprehension, little reason to cooperate, and no information about the afterlife beyond who is in the world of the dead.

entries.title: The Infernal and Necromancy
entries.summary: A botched attempt to summon or speak to the dead usually draws a malevolent spirit that impersonates the target and subtly corrupts what it says; Hermetic magic cannot see through the deception.
quotes: If a character botches when attempting to summon or speak to the dead, a likely result is that a malevolent spirit pretends to be the intended target.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal (Infernal ghosts)

entries.title: Finding En-Dor
entries.summary: Locating the true site of En-Dor takes a season of searching and a roll that is harder if the searcher is not in the field; teams use the leader's scores with a bonus for similarly skilled helpers, and rival groups are resolved by the higher total.
quotes: To Find En-Dor: Int + Area Lore Canaan + stress die vs. Ease Factor 18 (or 21 if not in the field)
To search among the various possible locations to find the true location of En-Dor takes one season.

entries.title: Books
entries.summary: Gives study sources for improving Area Lore Canaan: the Bible and Mishna count as tractatus, and several classical works are listed as summae or tractatus with their own Source Quality and level; poor translations lower the Source Quality.
quotes: both the Bible and the Mishna (a Jewish work) may be studied as if they were tractatus of Source Quality 5

entries.title: The Clay Tablets
entries.summary: Decoding the Canaanite clay tablets takes a season and a roll, after which each full sequence works as a summa for Area Lore Canaan whose Source Quality drops for every missing tablet; each tablet is an Arcane Connection to the others in its sequence.
quotes: A season's worth of decoding work is represented by a roll of Intelligence + Hebrew against an Ease Factor of 18.
the Source Quality is reduced by 3 for each missing tablet

entries.title: En-Dor Regio Level One
entries.summary: First regio level of En-Dor: a Divine aura swamps a lesser Magic aura, and a magical stream gives a Longevity Ritual effect while in the regio, forces an Aging roll on leaving, and yields tainted Aquam vis.
quotes: acts like a +5 Longevity Ritual (ArM5, page 101)

entries.title: En-Dor Regio Level Two
entries.summary: Second regio level of En-Dor: a strong Magic aura, a valley that cannot be left except through the cave, and a city of the dead that is a suitable covenant site.

entries.title: Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: Short account of what the ancient Canaanite necromancers could do beyond Hermetic limits, such as affecting the dead at any range and creating Arcane Connections to them easily, and why the Order fears their rediscovery.

entries.title: Mythic Herbalism Ease Factor Table
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for the healing effects, poisons and physical-bonus potions that a Mythic Herbalism user can brew.

entries.title: Mythic Herbalism
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability for brewing healing poultices, poisons and potions of physical bonuses: preparation time scales with the Ease Factor, extra doses raise the Ease Factor, and an Intelligence + Mythic Herbalism roll decides success. Describes expiry, duration and stacking limits.
quotes: a number of days equal to one-third the Ease Factor of the intended effect
the Ease Factor is increased by one for each additional dose
roll the character's Intelligence + Mythic Herbalism against the target Ease Factor

entries.title: Learned Magician Training
entries.summary: Learned magicians learn from a master then study from texts written under the normal text rules.

entries.title: Lore of the Mathematici
entries.summary: Describes the Organization Lore of the Mathematici of Bologna and what a character with it knows.

entries.title: Mythic Alchemy and Mythic Herbalism (Learned Magician Virtues)
entries.requires: Virtue: Mythic Alchemy or Mythic Herbalism
entries.summary: The opening of the learned-magician Virtues, including the extended rules behind Mythic Alchemy (formulae, reagents, alterations, vis limits, craft preparation) and Mythic Herbalism (concoction Ease Factor table for healing, poisons and potions).
quotes: Briefly, a formula is invented in a season by acquiring 5 experience points.
At the end of the process, the player must roll the character's Intelligence + Mythic Herbalism against the target Ease Factor.

entries.title: Magic of the Learned Magicians (charms, amulets and chartae)
entries.summary: Overview of verbal charms, chartae and amulets, and how charm magic bypasses the Arcane Connection requirement but must still overcome Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Learned Magician Arts
entries.summary: Learned magicians have three Techniques and three Forms; every charm or amulet needs one of each, and unGifted characters need the matching Virtue for each Art.

entries.title: Learned Magician Techniques (Tueor, Succurro, Vulnero)
entries.summary: Describes the Tueor, Succurro and Vulnero Techniques, what each can and cannot do, and how they relate to Hermetic Rego, Creo and Perdo.

entries.title: Learned Magician Forms (Fortunam, Magicam, Salutem)
entries.summary: Describes the Fortunam, Magicam and Salutem Forms and their limits compared with Hermetic Arts.

entries.title: Mythic Alchemists Tradition
entries.summary: Overview of the mythic alchemist alternate tradition and its required Virtues, Flaws, Arts and Abilities.
quotes: Required Virtues and Flaws: Mythic Alchemy, Laboratory Magician, and No Text Casting

entries.title: Cunning-Folk Tradition
entries.summary: Overview of the cunning-folk alternate tradition and its required Virtues, Arts and Abilities.
quotes: Required Virtues: Mythic Herbalism and Entreat the Faerie Powers

entries.title: Cunning-Folk Magic
entries.summary: Cunning-folk use the learned magician mechanics with local-language charms, Craft: Charm replacing Artes Liberales in the Lab Total, no horoscope requirement and their own lab assistance rule.
quotes: The cunning-folk substitute the Craft: Charm Ability for Artes Liberales in their Laboratory Total when creating their devices.

entries.title: Books of the Lector Priests (Faerie Rite Wizards)
entries.requires: Tradition: Faerie Rite Wizards (Realms of Power: Faerie)
entries.summary: Lector priests were Faerie Rite Wizards whose books of rites hold closely related effects (Evocation, Grant, Weal, Ware, Woe) performed with the Ceremony Special Ability.
quotes: all priests had the Ceremony Special Ability (page 115)

entries.title: Even Ancient Egyptians Thought Monumental Tombs Were Weird
entries.summary: Explains that the tomb chapter assumes Magic-aligned practitioners while this chapter describes Faerie-aligned priests served by Magic-aligned artisans, and that artefacts from either system may be used.
quotes: Artefacts designed under either system should be used in a troupe's saga, as suits their stories.

entries.title: Reading the Books of Ritual
entries.summary: How a character performs an Ancient Egyptian rite from a book: a Communication + Coptic roll against a target based on effect level, ritual preparation and purity, a required Faerie aura, and reasons rites fail.
quotes: This may require a Communication + Leadership roll against a target of 3 + 1 per required follower.
the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)

entries.title: Egyptian Views of Vis
entries.summary: Describes the materials the Egyptians thought held heka, such as resin, gold, iron and deformed things, which tomb robbers often discard without realizing they are vis.
quotes: Resin, for example, was thought to contain heka that could be used for preservation magic

entries.title: Heka and Faerie-Based Egyptian Magic
entries.summary: Explains heka, the Egyptian name for vis and written spells, and that Egyptian religious magic is mainly Faerie-based, so flourishes such as dawn casting and animal sacrifice were not optional.
quotes: Egyptian religious magic differed from Hermetic magic in that it is primarily based on the Faerie, not Magical, realm.

entries.title: Egyptian Rites Without Realms of Power: Faerie
entries.summary: A Hermetic substitute for Faerie Rites: after a Communication + Coptic roll, the reader makes a casting total from Stamina, closest Form and Technique, and Aura, with a table of Fatigue loss and Warping by result; Egyptian books are treated as casting tablets.
quotes: the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll against an Ease Factor of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)
The speaker's casting total is: Stamina + closest Form + closest Technique + Aura + stress dice (modified by Virtues and Flaws)

entries.title: Statue Consecration
entries.summary: How chief lectors consecrate a new statue so a faerie inhabits it, by performing a ritual narrative that faeries feed on; the roll is aided by a Faerie aura. Sidebars give examples of animated models and the play of faeries against one another.
quotes: This requires a Communication + Folk Ken roll against a target of 18.

entries.title: Threatening the Gods
entries.summary: Describes the alternative Enchantment Faerie Rite Method in which a caster threatens to destroy a faerie and the world unless given what is demanded, and who used it.
quotes: The spell-caster threatened to destroy not only the faerie, but the entire world, unless given what was demanded.

entries.title: The Weakest and Commonest Ancient Magicians
entries.summary: Describes local-spirit priests like village witches and suggests ways to design them, such as Faerie Friend, Faerie Doctors or Faerie Bargainers, with their grave goods as Mystery quest goals.
quotes: Some of these priests of local gods could be designed as Faerie Doctors

entries.title: Writings of Those Who Threatened the Gods
entries.summary: Three kinds of recoverable texts: Enchant-scripts, threat scripts that add a bonus to a Rite's casting total, and Mystery initiation texts granting Virtues such as Puissant Enchantment.
quotes: These grant a bonus to the casting total of a particular Rite.

entries.title: The Book of Thoth
entries.summary: A character who reads the Book of Thoth can effortlessly cast almost any Hermetic spell but dies or fades into Twilight within a day, after which the Book is hidden again.
quotes: Within one day, however, they either die or fade into Twilight.

entries.title: Gruagach Training
entries.summary: Explains how gruagachan are taught and how they improve: through a master, vis, exposure or adventure, with Abilities (but not Arts) also raisable by practice.
quotes: gruagachan may not improve their Arts through practice

entries.title: Gruagach Abilities (Gruagach Lore and Pictish Language)
entries.summary: Describes Gruagach Lore and Pictish Language, the latter acting as the gruagach equivalent of Magic Theory and capping how high the gruagach's Arts may rise.
quotes: With a Pictish score of 1, a gruagach's Arts may not exceed a score of 5.

entries.title: Gruagach Arts
entries.summary: Introduces the gruagach Techniques and Forms; a caster needs both a Technique and a Form, and an unGifted gruagach needs the matching Virtue for each Art used.

entries.title: Gruagach Techniques (Give and Take)
entries.summary: Describes the Give and Take Techniques, which grant things to or remove things from a target, and how they relate to Hermetic Techniques.

entries.title: Gruagach Forms (Blessing, Curse, Shape, Vision)
entries.summary: Describes the four gruagach Forms and what each can do with Give and Take, including which Virtues Blessing cannot affect and the conditions attached to curses.

entries.title: Spirit Magic (gruagach sidebar)
entries.summary: States that gruagach magic cannot affect the dead or their spirits, and points to the Ars Goetica rules for characters who want to command spirits.
quotes: The magic of the gruagachan cannot affect the dead or their spirits.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.114 Ars Goetica

entries.title: Trollsynir Tradition
entries.requires: Tradition: Trollsynir (Virtue: Giant Blood, Flaw: No Tattoo Magic)
entries.summary: Overview of the Norse trollsynir, an alternate tradition using the gruagach Arts, with their required Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: Required Virtues and Flaws: Giant Blood, No Tattoo Magic

entries.title: Trollsynir Magic
entries.summary: Trollskap works like gruagach magic with the Jotnar language replacing Pictish and no tattoo magic; overuse turns the trollson into a troll via Warping, and Initiation Scripts favor heroic deeds.
quotes: Any requirement for a score in the Pictish language is replaced with the Jotnar language

entries.title: Kolduni Tradition
entries.summary: Overview of the pagan wizards of the Novgorod Tribunal who use the gruagach Arts, with the required Flaw and favored Abilities.
quotes: Required Flaws: No Tattoo Magic

entries.title: Koldun Magic
entries.summary: Koldun magic uses the gruagach mechanics with Koldovali Theory in place of Pictish, a wholly oral tradition, an Arcane Connection Range needing water, a Durable External Soul variant, and a faerie-based Warping progression.
quotes: except the Ability Koldovali Theory replaces Pictish Language in the relevant formulae
The kolduni have access to the Arcane Connection Range, which adds +4 Magnitudes to a spell's level.

entries.title: Faerie Powers
entries.requires: Faerie wizard: Faerie Method, Faerie Power and Sympathy Trait
entries.summary: Explains that Faerie Powers are Supernatural Abilities used only with a Faerie Method, and that each Power has a vulnerability chosen when it is gained.
quotes: Every Faerie Power is vulnerable to certain uncommon circumstances, such as when touching iron, running water, or salt, when in the Dominion, or when repeating the character's name three times.

entries.title: Beguile (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for commanding targets or altering their memories, perceptions and emotions; any Sympathy Trait appropriate to the memory, emotion or perception can apply.

entries.title: Conjure (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power creating solid glamours or transforming a target into something else; the caster needs Sympathy Traits for both the original and new forms, and glamours can defy ordinary space and end unpredictably.

entries.title: Dream (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for perceiving things from outside one's body and glimpsing the future; includes advice for storyguides on handling prophetic visions as vague good or bad omens tied to a symbol.

entries.title: Grant (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for blessing or cursing a target with Warping Points, temporary Virtues and Flaws, or temporary Sympathy Traits that cannot be increased and do not affect Faerie Rank.

related.text: Chapter 5: Touches of Faerie, Charms and Sympathetic Influence

entries.title: Portage (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for instant travel by faerie trods, moving the target and what is attached to it from one place to another.

entries.title: Ware (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for protecting a target with wards against chosen things; wards often need a second Sympathy Trait describing what is warded against, both used for the maximum level, and must penetrate Magic Resistance.
quotes: Use both of these Traits to determine the maximum level of the effect.

entries.title: Weal (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power that alters natural healing and aging for the duration, speeding recovery or slowing aging; cannot return a character to childhood.
quotes: This effect cannot cause a character to revert to childhood, nor can it affect a character who has not yet reached physical maturity.

entries.title: Woe (Faerie Power)
entries.summary: Faerie Power for inflicting wounds, Fatigue loss, aging and slowed healing that vanish when the effect ends.

entries.title: Ex Miscellanea Traditions
entries.summary: Introduces three simple Ex Miscellanea magical traditions that can be chosen for a maga, noting others are in Houses of Hermes: Societates.
quotes: House Ex Miscellanea is not at all unified, consisting of many different magical traditions.

entries.title: Beast Masters
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea: Beast Masters tradition
entries.summary: A tradition of summoning and controlling wild creatures; members get Animal Ken and a Minor Magical Focus with a group of animals, the Incompatible Arts Flaw, and a Virtue and Flaw balance of their own.
quotes: They must take at least one more Flaw to balance their Virtues, and then have only 8 points of Flaws available to them to buy another 8 points of Virtues.

entries.title: Summon Animals
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea: Beast Masters tradition
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability to summon mundane animals by an audible call; the Ability score sets the number and size of animals arriving, and a Communication + Summon Animals roll sets arrival time.
quotes: He must then make a Communication + Summon Animals roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: The Nemthengacha
entries.summary: Background of the Nemthengacha, an Ex Miscellanea tradition of Celtic and Scandinavian sorcerers who create animosity and dissent in listeners.
quotes: The Nemthengacha (singular: Nemthenga) are a sect of Ex Miscellanea magi who have the ability to create animosity and dissent in their listeners.

entries.title: Nemthengacha Powers
entries.summary: A Nemthenga receives Embitterment as a free Major Non-Hermetic Virtue, Deficient Technique Rego as a compulsory Major Flaw, and Subtle Magic as a free Minor Hermetic Virtue.
quotes: Each has the Major Hermetic Flaw: Deficient Technique Rego.

entries.title: Embitterment
entries.summary: A Major Supernatural Ability that turns a listener against a chosen target by conversation, with an Ease Factor by relationship and increases for hatred, loathing and longer duration; it can be cancelled by Vim, Mentem effects.
quotes: EMBITTERMENT ROLL: Communication + Embitterment + Stress Die
Increasing this animosity to hatred adds +3 to the Ease Factor.
consider the effective level of the embitterment to be equal to the Nemthenga's score in Embitterment times five

entries.title: Tempestaria (Weather Witch)
entries.summary: A Saxon weather-witch tradition using simple sympathetic tools, with Whistle Up The Wind as its Major Non-Hermetic Virtue, Affinity with Auram, and a Necessary Condition Flaw.
quotes: Major Hermetic Flaw: Necessary Condition (tools for their magic to work)

entries.title: Whistle Up The Wind
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability to create a wind of a chosen strength by whistling, with an Ease Factor table by strength, changeable with Communication + Music rolls, diminishing each sunset.
quotes: makes a Stamina + Whistle Up The Wind roll, against the Ease Factor listed in the table below

entries.title: The Language of Adam
entries.summary: Fluency in Adamic gives the speaker a lasting Arcane Connection to anything he can name or that is in earshot, and even partial knowledge boosts the Penetration multiplier against targets with Magic Resistance; naming something also shapes its destiny.
quotes: has at least a score of 5 in the Dead Language (Adamic) Ability
receives a +1 bonus to his Penetration multiplier whenever he uses his magic on a target with Magic Resistance

entries.title: Story Hook: The Language of Innocence
entries.summary: Option for a Gifted child raised without language influences to begin with a limited, undevelopable score in Dead Language (Adamic) that can be taught on to others.
quotes: may begin with a score of 2 in Dead Language (Adamic)

entries.title: The Tower of Babel
entries.summary: Describes the research route to Adamic: become fluent in two of the four ancient root languages and reconstruct their common ancestor, which also demands a minimum Area Lore for the region.
quotes: the character must first become fluent in two of these four ancient languages via linguistic research
gain the required Area Lore score of 5

entries.title: Linguistic Research
entries.requires: Fluency in two related languages and Area Lore for their homeland
entries.summary: Seasonal study of two related languages grants Exposure experience in their common ancestor, and the character can alternatively experiment as in Breakthrough research with roll modifiers, a Discovery result giving a big experience jump and a botch costing experience.
quotes: This gives the character two points of Exposure experience in the common language Ability
the player may modify the results of the experimentation roll by +1 or –1, to a maximum of +3 or –3

entries.title: Seeking Lost Babylon
entries.summary: Gaining the Area Lore needed for linguistic research means exploring ancient Babylonia, which takes many seasons of Practice.
quotes: It takes about 15 seasons of exploring Babylonia to gain a score of 5 in Area Lore (Ancient Mesopotamia) through Practice.

entries.title: Adamic Writing
entries.summary: A character fluent in Adamic who can also write may name things in writing, creating the same Arcane Connection as speaking the name; inscribing the mark of Cain additionally ties the target to Cain's destiny.
quotes: who have a score of 1 in Artes Liberales

entries.title: Finding Cain
entries.summary: Ways to learn Adamic from Cain: slow Exposure from his muttering, tutoring him by listening to his confessions, or coercing him with holy things, with the warning that slaying Cain passes his curse to the killer.
quotes: through exposure to Cain's bizarre manner of speaking, they can pick up experience points in the language

entries.title: Christian Mysticism
entries.requires: Character aligned with the Divine realm
entries.summary: Introduces the mystic as a personal, non-institutional path to God, distinguishes contemplative and monistic mysticism and their dangers, and states that mystics must be Divine-aligned and that their Warping takes the form of Divine Ascent.
quotes: Both forms of mysticism require the character to be aligned with the Divine realm.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Holy Traditions

entries.title: Contemplative Mysticism
entries.requires: Positive Pious Personality Trait; association with the Divine realm; no Sinful Personality Traits
entries.summary: Describes the contemplative path of imitating Christ and sets its entry requirements: a positive Pious trait, no Sinful traits and an association with the Divine realm.
quotes: the mystic must possess a positive Pious Personality Trait score

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40 Sinful Personality Traits

entries.title: Spiritual Paths and Revelations
entries.summary: A contemplative mystic gains new Virtues, Methods, Powers or Supernatural Abilities by following a Spiritual Path: a Path Total is set by the Revelation sought, reduced by the character's Pious score to a Path Target, and met by completing Quest Components of listed values.
quotes: Path Target = Path Total – score in Personality Trait Pious
Total Quest Component Values = Path Total

entries.title: Monistic Mysticism
entries.requires: Flaw: Visions or Major Virtue: True Faith; positive Pious trait; association with the Divine realm
entries.summary: Describes the monistic path, its entry requirements, and its Twilight-Prone-like effect that a single Warping Point forces a test for Divine Ascent, so the mystic learns from Warping experiences rather than Spiritual Paths.
quotes: requires the mystic to possess either the Flaw Visions or the Major Virtue True Faith

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Gloom

entries.title: Advantages of Pursuing Monistic Mysticism
entries.summary: Monistic mystics gain extra experience from practising Holy Abilities (equal to Concentration) and, after Divine Ascent, may roll to integrate a Revelation and choose a benefit such as keeping mundane experience, a new Virtue, substituting Dominion Lore for another Realm Lore, or accepting the Infernal as subordinate to the Divine.
quotes: Intelligence + Concentration + stress die vs. Warping Score + stress die (no botch)
gains experience points equal to her Concentration Ability score rather than 4 experience points

entries.title: Mystics (female religious)
entries.requires: Visions Flaw, or True Faith with the Understanding power
entries.summary: Explains how to represent a religious mystic in game terms: usually the Visions Flaw, or occasionally True Faith with Understanding and Meditation. Also covers how a bishop's (or pope's) acceptance of a nun's visions earns her a Reputation as a mystic.
quotes: In most case, the experiences of a religious mystic are covered by the Visions Flaw.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.34, 36, 37, 54

entries.title: False Visions
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on non-divine sources of apparent visions (Spirits of Deceit, deluded or feigning individuals, Magic auras, faeries) and on the difficulty of proving a vision genuine, including a magus investigating inside a Dominion aura.
quotes: It can be very difficult to prove whether or not a particular mystical experience is genuinely divine.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.38

entries.title: Damhadh-Duidsan (Ex Miscellanea Tradition)
entries.summary: Overview of the Ogam rune tradition that curses enemies and steals their life, with its compulsory Virtue and Flaw package.
quotes: Major Non-Hermetic Virtue: Shapechanging, Giant Blood, or Incantation

entries.title: Hermetic Haruspexes (Ex Miscellanea Tradition)
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea; Hermetic Haruspexes tradition
entries.summary: Overview of the Roman tradition of divination by inspecting the entrails of sacrificed animals, with its compulsory Virtue and Flaw package and its susceptibility to Twilight.
quotes: Major Non-Hermetic Virtue: Divination and Augury

entries.title: Karaites (Ex Miscellanea Tradition)
entries.summary: Overview of the Karaite Jewish tradition of holy magic, which may join the Order only if it practises holy magic, with its compulsory Virtue and Flaw package.
quotes: Major Non-Hermetic Virtue: Holy Magic

entries.title: Malocchi (Ex Miscellanea Tradition)
entries.summary: Overview of the Italian tradition of Entrancement through the gaze, with its compulsory Virtue and Flaw package and a required extra Virtue.
quotes: As well as his free Virtues and Flaws, a maloccho must also take Piercing Gaze as a compulsory Virtue.

entries.title: Scinnfolk (Gifted Companions Tradition)
entries.summary: Overview of the cunning-folk tradition of Gifted Companions who keep natural and faerie charms instead of Hermetic magic, with its Virtue and common Virtue and Flaw choices.
quotes: Major Non-Hermetic Virtue: Fertility (free with The Gift)

entries.title: Witches of Thessaly (Ex Miscellanea Tradition)
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea; Witches of Thessaly tradition
entries.summary: Overview of the Thessalian tradition of sorcery, necromancy and curses, with its compulsory Virtue and Flaw package and a note on its suspicion of diabolism.
quotes: Major Non-Hermetic Virtue: Summoning

entries.title: Heron's Art: Mechanica
entries.requires: Virtue: Mechanica of Heron, or Hermetic integration of Heron's Mechanica
entries.summary: Introduces the Mechanica of Heron Supernatural Virtue, how a Gifted character learns it from a surviving practitioner, and why a magus would rather integrate it into Hermetic theory.
quotes: A new Major Supernatural Virtue, Mechanica of Heron, represents the magical techniques described in this chapter.

entries.title: Integrating Heron's Mechanica into Hermetic Theory
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research (Mutable Device and Awakened Device)
entries.summary: Describes the two suggested Breakthroughs needed to fold Mechanica into Hermetic theory, and how uncorrupted texts and working mechanica give Insight and a one-time Lab Total bonus when inventing a matching device.
quotes: Integrating Heron's Mechanica requires the following two suggested Breakthroughs: Mutable Device and Awakened Device.
Mechanica provide a bonus equal to the magnitude of the device's effect.

related.text: Ancient Magic Introduction: Insight and breakthroughs

entries.title: Ability: Mechanica of Heron
entries.summary: The Supernatural Ability covering what mechanica are, how to build them and use them, mainly in the laboratory, with its suggested specialties.
quotes: Inventing Mechanica, Constructing Anima, working with a particular material.

entries.title: Mechanica of Heron: constructing mechanica
entries.summary: How a Mechanician builds and alters ordinary mechanica in a laboratory: a creation total against a creation level based on the effect's magnitude, modifiers for size and time to employ, a cost in Mythic Pounds rather than vis, and a week's study to alter a device's effect.
quotes: Construct Mechanica of Heron Total: Intelligence + Mechanica of Heron Ability + (lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales) + aura
Mechanica Creation Level: (3 x Magnitude of Imbued Effect) + modifiers
Creating Mechanica Cost: 1 Mythic Pound per 3 points of Mechanica Creation Level

related.text: ArM5 p.187 auras and magical devices

entries.title: Mechanica of Heron: awakened simulacra (anima)
entries.summary: Rules for building a simulacrum of an animal, working out its Magic Might from size and material, awakening its anima with a cumulative-bonus lab project, and playing the resulting sentient mechanica (traits, Abilities, powers of movement and speech).
quotes: Anima's Magic Might: Size + Material Base Points + (lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales)
Awaken Anima Total: Intelligence + Mechanica of Heron Ability + (lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales) + Aura
Awaken Anima Level: 9 + Magnitude of Anima's Magic Might

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.129 automata powers

entries.title: Mechanica of Heron
entries.summary: Introduces the Mechanica of Heron as both a Major Supernatural Virtue and its Supernatural Ability, letting a character build magical wonders and sentient animae. Mechanicians can also make permanent enchantments without vis and build devices whose effects can later be changed within the same Technique and Form pairing.
quotes: Mechanica of Heron refers to both a Major Supernatural Virtue and its attendant Supernatural Ability.

entries.title: Summoning Aspects of Fimbulwinter (Utiseta)
entries.summary: The Muspelli release Aspects of the primal cold by performing a special utiseta at an Irminsul, using Intelligence and Muspelli Lore like the Jotun patron summoning, with extra modifiers from the Irminsul and the patron's elements. Gives the Ease Factor, typical Power Modifier and what happens when an Aspect is reduced to 0 Might.
quotes: with an Ease Factor of 50
The Irminsul used in the utiseta provides an additional Power Modifier of 1, cumulative with all the standard ones.
Reducing an Aspect to 0 Might doesn't destroy it, but forces it to return to the Magic Realm, where it could be summoned again.

related.text: Rival Magic p.9 and p.85 Muspelli Magic Defenses

entries.title: Researching Muspelli Magic as a Hermetic Breakthrough
entries.summary: Describes how magi can investigate Fimbulwinter and the Muspelli tradition, and notes that integrating utiseta-style casting into Hermetic Theory counts as a Hermetic Breakthrough giving an alternative for ceremonial casting.
quotes: This last option represents a Hermetic Breakthrough, representing the integration of the utiseta-style casting method as an alternative for ceremonial casting.

entries.title: Hunting the Muspelli: Arcane Connections to the Jotnar
entries.summary: Explains that the threat ends only when every Muspelli who knows the summoning ritual is dead, that the ritual can be passed on in a season of instruction, and how an Arcane Connection to a Jotun patron can be used against all its Muspelli.
quotes: a process which takes a season of instruction
Once dead, Muspelli are no longer Arcane Connections to their Jotun patron.

entries.title: Destroying Irminsul and Using Them as Arcane Connections
entries.summary: Destroying an Irminsul removes the Arcane Connection the Muspelli need for summoning Aspects, but the surviving Irminsul can also be used by magi as a lasting Arcane Connection to the currently summoned Aspect.
quotes: the Irminsul is considered an indefinite Arcane Connection

entries.title: Daimon of Fimbulwinter and Perdo Vim
entries.summary: Rules guidance on striking at the Daimon of Fimbulwinter in the Magic Realm: it is effectively immortal there and immune to Perdo Vim, while summoned Aspects can be destroyed but not eradicated.
quotes: It cannot be damaged by Perdo Vim effects the way other creatures with Might are vulnerable.

entries.title: Gandar and Utiseta (Storing and Casting Utiseta)
entries.summary: Explains how a Muspelli stores an utiseta effect in a gandur for quick use, the limits on storage time and on fixing the target at casting, and when the Casting Total and Penetration are rolled and what failure or botch does.
quotes: a gandur can only store an effect for one year
A failure on this roll means that nothing happens, and the energy gathered is safely dissipated

related.text: Rival Magic p.90 Penetration of utiseta
Rival Magic p.91 storing utiseta in a gandur and Warping

entries.title: Faerie Bargaining (Ars Fabulosa)
entries.requires: Faerie Bargaining: one of the Virtues Summoning, Bonding, Captivating or Dismissing
entries.summary: Introduces the Ars Fabulosa, the hedge art of bargaining with faeries through four powers (Summoning, Bonding, Captivating, Dismissing) that start at score 0, increase like Arts, and are learned as Supernatural Abilities or from Virtues.
quotes: There are four powers associated with bargaining: Summoning, Bonding, Captivating, and Dismissing.

related.text: Chapter 5: Touches of Faerie, Learning Faerie Abilities

entries.title: Summoning (Faerie Bargaining)
entries.summary: Procedure for summoning a faerie: Sympathy Traits cap the Might that can be summoned, a Fatigue level is spent, a Summoning Total is rolled against the faerie's Might and Magic Resistance, and success holds the faerie to listen and bargain; covers botches, specific faeries, failure, and the experience and penalty for keeping or breaking a bargain.
quotes: Summoning Total: stress die + Presence + Summoning + Faerie Rank + aura Maximum Might
The sum of these Traits, multiplied by 5, determines the maximum Might Score that the character can summon.

entries.title: Bonding (Faerie Bargaining)
entries.summary: Power forming a mystic bond with a faerie, using a Bonding Total against the faerie's Might and Magic Resistance, which lets the bearer use the faerie's Characteristics, powers, a shared enchanted effect, or protections from Warping and hardship; bonds to objects need a charm and only one bond can be held at a time.
quotes: Bonding Total: stress die + Communication + Bonding + Faerie Rank + aura
Maximum Might Score: (Sympathy Traits x 5)

entries.title: Faerie Bargains
entries.requires: Faerie Bargaining: one of the Virtues Summoning, Bonding, Captivating or Dismissing
entries.summary: Guidance on conducting a bargaining session with a faerie: working out what it wants with Intelligence + Faerie Lore, roleplaying etiquette, a contested roll to resolve a stalled session, and typical offers and requests.
quotes: you can quickly resolve the bargaining session with a contested Communication + Bargain roll, modified by the character's Faerie Rank.

entries.title: Captivating (Faerie Bargaining)
entries.summary: Power for exchanging places with a faerie, with a Captivating Total against the faerie's Might and Magic Resistance; covers what is exchanged, struggles for dominance, and the Warping Points gained.
quotes: Captivating Total: stress die + Perception + Captivating + Faerie Rank + aura

entries.title: Dismissing (Faerie Bargaining)
entries.summary: Power for cancelling effects made by beings with Might, ending effects on them, or releasing them from supernatural agreements, using a Dismissing Total limited by Sympathy Traits; can deflect powers and dismiss several effects with a cumulative penalty.
quotes: Dismissing Total: stress die + Intelligence + Dismissing + Faerie Rank + aura

entries.title: Vampire Hunters
entries.summary: Introduces vampire hunters as specially touched humans whose magic works on all supernatural creatures, who arise by birth circumstances, vampire parentage or Hermetic training (fector).

entries.title: The Sabotnik (Saturday-born hunters)
entries.requires: Born on a Saturday or during the Unclean Days or Wolf Holiday
entries.summary: Describes the sabotnik, who is born on a Saturday and so is immune to the direct powers of vampires bound by that taboo, can sense vampires and magicians, and may be fated to become a vampire. Notes the option to randomly determine birth days.
quotes: Anyone born on a Saturday is therefore immune to the direct powers of such vampire.

entries.title: The Glog (vampire-protecting hunters)
entries.requires: Born feet first, with teeth or with red hair
entries.summary: Describes the glog, a hunter specialising in protecting people from vampires, who crafts defensive weapons from black hawthorn and is usually aggressive and physically gifted.

entries.title: Black Hawthorn (Shape and Material Bonuses)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the Shape and Material bonuses of black hawthorn for enchanting, notably a protection-from-vampires bonus.
quotes: Protection from vampires +7 Protection from evil +4 Prevent disease +4

entries.title: The Dhampir (child of a vampire)
entries.requires: Being a child of a vampire (Dhampir Virtue)
entries.summary: Describes dhampiri, the hunters sired by vampires, who charge a fee that by tradition cannot be bargained down and who will themselves rise as vampires after death unless precautions are taken.
quotes: dhampiri carry a dark secret: that they themselves will become vampires following their death

entries.title: The Vampirdzhi (son of a vampire)
entries.summary: Describes vampirdzhia, sons of vampires who become hunters out of necessity rather than tradition, may be trained, and also risk rising as vampires after death.
quotes: Only men are believed to be vampirdzhia; the daughters of vampires become witches instead.

entries.title: Wondrous Items (craftsman-made minor enchantments)
entries.summary: How a craftsman with Touched by (Realm) makes a non-Hermetic wondrous item for a specific customer: limits on its single effect, its Craft Level built from a base plus the magnitude and daily uses, how Workshop Total progress accumulates over seasons, helper limits, Arcane Connection to the recipient and verbal triggers.
quotes: Base Supernatural Item Craft Level: 12 + Magnitude of Hermetic Effect + Modifier for Number of Uses per Day
To create wondrous items, a character must have the Major Supernatural Virtue Touched by (Realm).
Wondrous items have no Penetration scores and cannot affect anyone with even the slightest Magic Resistance.

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus chart

entries.title: Craftsmen Supernatural Virtues (Eye of Hephaestus, Touched by (Realm), Crafter's Healing)
entries.requires: Virtue: Eye of Hephaestus, Touched by (Realm) or Crafter's Healing
entries.summary: Sidebar describing three craftsman-only Supernatural Virtues and the rolls they use: judging an item's quality and magic, enabling wondrous items, and the Crafter's Healing Ability for healing wounds at a cost in fatigue and Warping.
quotes: make a Perception + Awareness + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Make a Presence + Crafter's Healing + stress die roll against an Ease Factor equal to the Improvement Ease Factor determined by the Wound Recovery Table (ArM5, page 179).

entries.title: Crafters of Wondrous Items
